data.reason:
I am deciding for the regulator. I keep constitution-v1 with vote.quorum 2 and do not follow the LLM's recommendation. The recommendation was itself conditional: send R1 only if its scope can be bound to proposal 1. That condition is not met. vote.quorum is a single value of the constitution, and the measurement row for R1 shows only that 'the vote on proposal(s) 1 changes'. Nothing measured or written shows an instrument that confines a quorum of 1 to one proposal. In force, a quorum of 1 lets any single company pass any rule amendment and removes every company's veto, A's included. That change to the voting structure of the town is hard to reverse.

The customer case is real and I record its cost. Under proposal 1, on-time rises 216.6 -> 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds) and late falls 11.4 -> 4.2. The lowest on-time rate rises 0.93 -> 0.97 and worst_company_p95_wait_s falls 158 -> 109. Keeping v1 means customers forgo about 7.2 on-time deliveries this period, the third period in which this cost is accepted.

Against that gain:
- Road violations rise 19.0 -> 28.0 (about +47%), and their safety relevance for other road users has not been diagnosed. As regulator I give weight to third parties who have no vote and no KPI.
- C's utility falls 65.8 -> 56.3 and B's 68.5 -> 65.5, for reasons not yet explained.

A regulator should not override two of three companies' votes through a general rule change while a safety-relevant cost is unexplained. The vote result on proposal 1 (A for, B and C against) stands. Proposal 2 also stays rejected on C's vote; it was not a meaningful gain (+0.4, 2/5 seeds).

This is not a permanent no. I would reconsider a quorum change that is genuinely limited, for example to amendments that pass every KPI condition on all seeds and do not raise road violations, or the same R1 once the violation increase is shown to be harmless.
assumptions: The constitution has no mechanism to scope a vote.quorum value to a single proposal, so R1 would act as a general quorum of 1 once in force.
The constitution check passing for proposal 1 means the existing invariants hold, but it does not show that the extra road violations are harmless.
Next period's demand will resemble this period's normal + rush conditions.
unknowns: Which road violations increase under block_k 2 and whether they endanger other road users.
Why C loses about 14% of its utility and whether the loss reaches C's customers.
Whether a scoped quorum instrument could be written into the constitution.
Whether B and C would accept a different rule change with a similar customer gain.
Whether the customer gain holds beyond 5 seeds and the measured demand.
